kind: inspect_data (accounting integrity of the lead candidate; not a new strategy or variant)
question: Does pairing MEXC prices with Binance funding (the development and untouched-holdout construction) overstate the multi-premia blend, compared with MEXC prices and MEXC funding (the forward construction)?
registration_note: Declared 2026-10-06 after fast-gates-v1 G3 (MIXED: the XS legs did not replicate on Binance prices). MEXC's public funding history starts 2025-04-15, so the full 2020-26 rebuild is impossible; the test is a paired comparison on the window MEXC covers. Rules frozen, nothing tuned.

data.prices: MEXC 8h klines from the existing caches (%TEMP%/multi_premia_data.pkl: 70 development coins; %TEMP%/multi_premia_untouched_data.pkl: 60 untouched coins), unchanged
data.funding_A: Binance funding from the same caches (as in the development and holdout runs)
data.funding_B: MEXC realized funding (contract/funding_rate/history) from 2025-04-15; before that, funding_A is spliced in so the warm-up is identical

method: Frozen multi-premia-blend-v1 rules (S1 trend, S2 XS momentum, S3 XS carry, S4 equal-risk blend, 20 bps round trip), run twice on identical prices: A with funding_A, B with funding_B. Report annualized return, Sharpe and Newey-West t per leg for A and B, the paired daily difference B-A with its NW t, and the correlation of MEXC vs Binance funding per coin.

reading_rules.MATERIAL: S4 annual return under B is below 50% of that under A, or the paired S4 difference B-A has NW t <= -2: the funding mismatch inflates the historical evidence; development (2.09) and holdout (1.39) Sharpe are not decision-grade
reading_rules.NOT_MATERIAL: otherwise: the funding source is not the explanation, and the G3 gap comes from MEXC vs Binance price paths themselves
reading_rules.scope: applied separately to the 70 development coins (primary) and the 60 untouched coins (secondary)
